# Concept Kernel Protocol (CKP)
# https://conceptkernel.org

## What is this?
An open protocol for sovereign, semantic, self-governing state. A concept kernel is a place where meaning lives and is answerable for itself: it declares what kinds of things exist for it (RDF classes with SHACL shapes), accepts only facts that honour those declarations, stamps every fact with who made it (createdBy), whose law governed it (producedBy), at which version of that law (sealedAtEpoch) and under which shape it was judged (conformsToShape), and changes its law only by the agreement of those who live under it (propose → vote → apply). Its only interface is one verified door: clients speak NATS over /wss; the relay behind the door calls the substrate's one SQL function, ckp.dispatch(verb, payload). No REST, no query surface.

## Current version
CKP v3.12 — "Self-Moving, Never Self-Ruling". The kernel notices what its participants care about (sealed Signals: assent, dissent, implicit dwell), derives Scores under weights that are themselves bounded law, and drafts its own next change when a score crosses its threshold — the tick never votes, applies, or advances an epoch. Each kernel keeps its own clock (orbit law: period, lead, anchor; the next crossing is computable from sealed law). Ownership is immovable, quorum follows the project's declared kind, only the owner enacts, in-kernel roles narrow and never widen, every refusal carries a registered code, every routed verb carries a sealed declaration, and every stored digest names its method.
- Law: https://conceptkernel.org/ontology/v3.12/core.ttl — sha256 2e90a6512c7aae567714be69b92b37af4393e8da8d65a05c047c5d51e1bed07b (sidecar wave-3.12-pass-3); 30 classes, 31 NodeShapes, 102 properties
- Namespace: https://conceptkernel.org/ontology/v3.11/core# (the v3.12 law binds the v3.11 namespace deliberately; the law carries the version, the IRIs stay stable)
- Runtime: pgCK 0.4.112 (PostgreSQL 18 extension, attested) — https://github.com/styk-tv/pgCK
- Engine: pgRDF 0.6.34 (RDF / SHACL / SPARQL / OWL-RL inside PostgreSQL) — https://github.com/styk-tv/pgRDF
- Client: cklib, served by every door at /cklib/ — https://github.com/ConceptKernel/CK.Lib.Js
- Bundle: ghcr.io/sporaxis-com/ociger-ck-allinone:v0.7.45 (index sha256:9d18e2b0d6ae1646f22582dbdd25e8e5c1cd9e99862b741e7a6d04f73092707d) — https://github.com/sporaxis-com/oci-germination

## The distinction the protocol rests on
A caller reaches a kernel through a VERB, not a query surface. A query surface (SQL/SPARQL/GraphQL/ORM) lets the caller author logic the engine runs — unbounded, unenumerable. A verb is a finite, named, pre-declared operation with a typed payload the engine knows before it runs. Even query-shaped verbs bind typed parameters into logic sealed by governance. This is what makes grants enumerable and shapes unbypassable.

- v3.4 (2026 Q1): 79 classes, 4 pages — the grounding
- v3.5 (2026 Q1): 97 classes, 21 pages — three loops as Description Logic boxes
- v3.6 (2026 Q2): 119 classes, 37 pages — the full specification
- v3.7 (2026 Q2): 120 classes, 9 shapes, 31 pages, 20 checks, 5 edge predicates — the refined canon
- v3.8: the first permanent core namespace
- v3.9 / v3.9.1 (2026 Q2): Critical Isolation — one door, a closed verb vocabulary, the role floor
- v3.10: CKN, the notation — parked
- v3.11 (2026 Q3): Where Declaring Becomes Binding — a self-contained root, 27 classes, 27 shapes, every constraint measured enforcing
- v3.12 (2026 Q3): Self-Moving, Never Self-Ruling — 30 classes, 31 shapes; signals, scores, the kernel's own clock, scopes, and the floors that hold them
